passages.text: Remember your Creator in the days of your youth, before the days of adversity come and the years approach of which you will say, “I find no pleasure in them,” before the light of the sun, moon, and stars is darkened, and the clouds return after the rain, on the day the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men stoop, when those grinding cease because they are few and those watching through windows see dimly, when the doors to the street are shut and the sound of the mill fades away, when one rises at the sound of a bird and all the daughters of song grow faint, when men fear the heights and dangers of the road, when the almond tree blossoms, the grasshopper loses its spring, and the caper berry shrivels— for then man goes to his eternal home and mourners walk the streets.
passages.sermon:
Remember your Creator while you are young.
Do this before hard days come.
Do this before years arrive when you say, “I find no joy in them.”
Do this before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars grow dark.
Do this before clouds return after the rain.
There will be a day when the keepers of the house tremble.
There will be a day when strong men bend down.
There will be a day when the women who grind grain stop because they are few.
There will be a day when those who look through the windows see darkness.
There will be a day when the doors to the street are closed.
The sound of the mill will grow quiet.
People will rise at the sound of a bird.
All the daughters of song will grow weak.
People will fear heights.
People will fear dangers on the road.
The almond tree will blossom.
The grasshopper will drag itself along.
The caper berry will fail.
At that time, a person goes to his eternal home.
Mourners walk in the streets.
passages.original: וּזְכֹר֙ אֶת־ בּ֣וֹרְאֶ֔יךָ בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא־ יָבֹ֙אוּ֙ יְמֵ֣י הָֽרָעָ֔ה וְהִגִּ֣יעוּ שָׁנִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמַ֔ר אֵֽין־ לִ֥י בָהֶ֖ם חֵֽפֶץ׃ עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־ תֶחְשַׁ֤ךְ הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ וְהָא֔וֹר וְהַיָּרֵ֖חַ וְהַכּוֹכָבִ֑ים וְשָׁ֥בוּ הֶעָבִ֖ים אַחַ֥ר הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃ בַּיּ֗וֹם שֶׁיָּזֻ֙עוּ֙ שֹׁמְרֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת וְהִֽתְעַוְּת֖וּ אַנְשֵׁ֣י הֶחָ֑יִל וּבָטְל֤וּ הַטֹּֽחֲנוֹת֙ כִּ֣י מִעֵ֔טוּ וְחָשְׁכ֥וּ הָרֹא֖וֹת בָּאֲרֻבּֽוֹת׃ וְסֻגְּר֤וּ דְלָתַ֙יִם֙ בַּשּׁ֔וּק בִּשְׁפַ֖ל ק֣וֹל הַֽטַּחֲנָ֑ה וְיָקוּם֙ לְק֣וֹל הַצִּפּ֔וֹר וְיִשַּׁ֖חוּ כָּל־ בְּנ֥וֹת הַשִּֽׁיר׃ גַּ֣ם מִגָּבֹ֤הַּ יִרָ֙אוּ֙ וְחַתְחַתִּ֣ים בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְיָנֵ֤אץ הַשָּׁקֵד֙ וְיִסְתַּבֵּ֣ל הֶֽחָגָ֔ב וְתָפֵ֖ר הָֽאֲבִיּוֹנָ֑ה כִּֽי־ הֹלֵ֤ךְ הָאָדָם֙ אֶל־ בֵּ֣ית עוֹלָמ֔וֹ וְסָבְב֥וּ בָשּׁ֖וּק הַסֹּפְדִֽים׃

passages.text: Remember Him before the silver cord is snapped and the golden bowl is crushed, before the pitcher is shattered at the spring and the wheel is broken at the well, before the dust returns to the ground from which it came and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
passages.sermon:
God created you.
God gave you life.
Remember God while you are alive.
Do this before your life ends.
One day, the silver cord will snap.
One day, the golden bowl will break.
The pitcher will shatter at the spring.
The wheel will break at the well.
Your body will return to the dust of the earth.
Your spirit will return to God, who gave it.
passages.original: עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־ יִרְחַק חֶ֣בֶל הַכֶּ֔סֶף וְתָרֻ֖ץ גֻּלַּ֣ת הַזָּהָ֑ב וְתִשָּׁ֤בֶר כַּד֙ עַל־ הַמַּבּ֔וּעַ וְנָרֹ֥ץ הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל אֶל־ הַבּֽוֹר׃ וְיָשֹׁ֧ב הֶעָפָ֛ר עַל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָ֑ה וְהָר֣וּחַ תָּשׁ֔וּב אֶל־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְתָנָֽהּ׃

passages.text: “Futility of futilities,” says the Teacher. “Everything is futile!”
passages.sermon:
The Teacher speaks.
The Teacher is wise.
The Teacher says, “Futility of futilities.”
Everything is futile.
passages.original: הֲבֵ֧ל הֲבָלִ֛ים אָמַ֥ר הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת הַכֹּ֥ל הָֽבֶל׃

passages.text: Not only was the Teacher wise, but he also taught the people knowledge; he pondered, searched out, and arranged many proverbs.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher was wise.
The Teacher taught the people knowledge.
The Teacher pondered many things.
The Teacher searched out many things.
The Teacher arranged many proverbs.
passages.original: וְיֹתֵ֕ר שֶׁהָיָ֥ה קֹהֶ֖לֶת חָכָ֑ם ע֗וֹד לִמַּד־ דַּ֙עַת֙ אֶת־ הָעָ֔ם וְאִזֵּ֣ן וְחִקֵּ֔ר תִּקֵּ֖ן מְשָׁלִ֥ים הַרְבֵּֽה׃

passages.text: The Teacher searched to find delightful sayings and to record accurate words of truth.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher was wise.
The Teacher searched for delightful sayings.
The Teacher wanted to find words that please people.
The Teacher wrote words that are true.
The Teacher recorded words that are accurate.
passages.original: בִּקֵּ֣שׁ קֹהֶ֔לֶת לִמְצֹ֖א דִּבְרֵי־ חֵ֑פֶץ וְכָת֥וּב יֹ֖שֶׁר דִּבְרֵ֥י אֱמֶֽת׃

passages.text: The words of the wise are like goads, and the anthologies of the masters are like firmly embedded nails driven by a single Shepherd.
passages.sermon:
Wise people speak important words.
Their words are like goads.
Goads are sharp sticks that guide animals.
The collections of wise teachers are like nails.
These nails are firmly fixed in place.
One Shepherd gives these words and collections.
passages.original: דִּבְרֵ֤י חֲכָמִים֙ כַּדָּ֣רְבֹנ֔וֹת וּֽכְמַשְׂמְר֥וֹת נְטוּעִ֖ים בַּעֲלֵ֣י אֲסֻפּ֑וֹת נִתְּנ֖וּ מֵרֹעֶ֥ה אֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: And by these, my son, be further warned: There is no end to the making of many books, and much study wearies the body.
passages.sermon:
The Teacher speaks to his son.
He gives a warning.
He says, “Be careful.”
People make many books.
There is no end to this.
Studying too much makes the body tired.
passages.original: וְיֹתֵ֥ר מֵהֵ֖מָּה בְּנִ֣י הִזָּהֵ֑ר עֲשׂ֨וֹת סְפָרִ֤ים הַרְבֵּה֙ אֵ֣ין קֵ֔ץ וְלַ֥הַג הַרְבֵּ֖ה יְגִעַ֥ת בָּשָֽׂר׃

passages.text: When all has been heard, the conclusion of the matter is this: Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives the final conclusion of the book of Ecclesiastes.
The speaker is a wise teacher.
He has considered everything in life.
He says, “Here is the end of the matter.”
He says, “We have heard everything.”
He gives a clear command.
He says, “Fear God.”
He says, “Keep God’s commandments.”
He explains why this is important.
He says, “This is the whole duty of every person.”
passages.original: ס֥וֹף דָּבָ֖ר הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁמָ֑ע אֶת־ הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים יְרָא֙ וְאֶת־ מִצְוֺתָ֣יו שְׁמ֔וֹר כִּי־ זֶ֖ה כָּל־ הָאָדָֽם׃

passages.text: For God will bring every deed into judgment, along with every hidden thing, whether good or evil.
passages.sermon:
God will judge every action.
God will judge every hidden thing.
God will judge what is good.
God will judge what is evil.
passages.original: כִּ֤י אֶת־ כָּל־ מַֽעֲשֶׂ֔ה הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים יָבִ֥א בְמִשְׁפָּ֖ט עַ֣ל כָּל־ נֶעְלָ֑ם אִם־ ט֖וֹב וְאִם־ רָֽע׃
